subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should the bundled Slack plugin support user-authorized `message.im` events and reply-as-user delivery through xoxp tokens, and if so what explicit opt-in and audit boundaries are required?
rationale: The requested behavior changes Slack identity, token authority, and outbound attribution; code inspection can show it is missing, but only maintainers can approve that security/product boundary.

options.title: Add explicit user-identity mode
options.body: Keep bot-token behavior as default and add a clearly documented, live-proven opt-in that routes by Slack authorizations and sends with the selected user token only inside that mode.

options.title: Decline bundled support
options.body: Keep OpenClaw’s bundled Slack plugin bot/app-authored and ask users who need full user impersonation to build or run a dedicated custom Slack integration outside core.

options.title: Broaden existing userToken behavior
options.body: Treat `userTokenReadOnly: false` as permission to receive and send user-authorized DMs, accepting the larger upgrade and security blast radius.

recommendation.title: Add explicit user-identity mode
recommendation.body: Keep bot-token behavior as default and add a clearly documented, live-proven opt-in that routes by Slack authorizations and sends with the selected user token only inside that mode.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Slack runtime and monitor ownership signals make this the best available routing candidate for the security-sensitive Slack channel decision.
